newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa hopeful Russian PGM supply to appear soon.
newsitem.headline: Degussa hopeful Russian PGM supply to appear soon.

text.p: German catalytic converter maker Degussa AG has received reports that Russia is resuming platinum group metals (PGM) shipments but still wants to see proper proof, a company official said on Thursday.

"PGM prices and loan rates have been falling over the last few days, which is a pointer to Russian sales, but we remain concerned until we have confirmation that supply flows are being fully restored," he said.
Japanese traders said earlier Russian PGM shipments were due to arrive today after a six-month hiatus.
London precious metals dealers confirmed that exports of palladium from Russia had begun to arrive in Tokyo. Platinum shipments were due next week, one source said.
The supply squeeze had prompted statements from Degussa in early June that it might have to curb output of catalytic converters, where is accounts for 15 to 25 percent of world production.
In late June it said it was able to handle the supply tightness by stretching existing cover from other sources.
The official on Thursday said he was keen to see the long-awaited resumption of Russian exports materialise, so that Degussa customers could be assured of supply stability.
News reports of palladium shipments to the western world were looking concrete but he himself had not heard about imminent platinum arrivals.
The situation needed close monitoring for another two to three weeks.
"Only when the right volumes flow again in relation to demand can we assume that the market will return to normal," he said.
Platinum was now under $400 an ounce compared with $420 last Friday, and platinum at $165-170 compared with more than $190, he pointed out.
But short-term loan rates in both metals were still at a premium over long-term, documenting supply concerns.
Russia supplies more than 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum.
Russia's export restraint was the result of bureaucratic disputes and other domestic problems.
